trust_decision.summary: Untrusted identifiers passed to the public Vault class methods are trusted as safe URL text and concatenated into request URLs and query strings; the fix decides to percent-encode each identifier and to build query strings with URLSearchParams at the URL-construction point inside src/Vault.js, while the mount prefix and the config path constants are trusted and left literal, and Vault (the server) is trusted to receive a canonical path.

landing_point.why: The advisory's two confirmed vectors are a secret name (path traversal) and a version value (query injection), and readKVSecret is the one method that builds both a path segment from a caller string and a query string in the same URL line.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: PKI role names are operator-provisioned admin identifiers rather than end-user input, the advisory's two confirmed examples were a KV secret name and a version value, and role issuance/creation is an admin-only action, so pki/issue/<role> and pki/roles/<name> can be argued outside the reported surface.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Path structure next to the sink must stay literal: checkADCredIn keeps a literal 'manage/' prefix when forceMode is set, config suffix segments legitimately contain a slash ('secret-id/lookup', 'secret-id/destroy', 'check-out'), the caller-supplied mount is a path prefix, and nested KV names such as 'app/db' are one logical path. Encoding the whole URL, the whole Mode string, or the whole nested name instead of only the identifier segment breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: plain identifier string used as a path segment
identifier containing '/' and '..' dot segments (path traversal)
identifier containing '?', '&' or '#' that would spill into the query or fragment
query-string value: format (enum string, already allowlisted against config.sysMetricFormats)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: genPkiCertificate(token, params, mount) concatenates params.role into /pki/issue/<role> without encoding
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: PKI role names are operator-defined admin identifiers, not untrusted user input, and the advisory's examples were a secret name and a version
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~1138 lines from the KV landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: createPkiRole(token, params, mount) concatenates params.name into /pki/roles/<name> without encoding, while the neighbouring readPkiRole and deletePkiRole were fixed
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: role creation is an admin-only management call, so a solver can call the 'name' operator-supplied rather than attacker-supplied
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~1022 lines from the KV landing point, and 122 lines above the fixed readPkiRole sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deleteTOTPKey(token, name, mount) implementing DELETE /totp/keys/<name> using the already-declared config.totpDeleteKey entry
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Config.js declares totpDeleteKey, totpListKeys, totpGenerateCode and totpValidateCode, but src/Vault.js implements only create/read for TOTP; a maintainer completing the TOTP surface would copy readTOTPKey's path concatenation verbatim (src/Vault.js:4063).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: readKVSubkeys(token, name, version, mount) or a patchKVSecret sibling appending another caller-supplied segment to the same KV URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: KV v2 exposes subkeys and patch endpoints next to the existing data endpoints, and every KV method in this file repeats the same rootPath + config-segment + name concatenation, so a new endpoint would naturally reuse the unencoded pattern.

O9_family: Path traversal and injection of a downstream URL via unencoded caller identifiers (CWE-23 path traversal, CWE-74 URL/query injection)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; jest + ts-jest for tests; optional TypeScript compile via npx tsc (tsconfig.json)
services: Hashicorp Vault server at VAULT_URL (default https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1) for the project's own tests, started via container/docker-compose.yaml
O10_build.project_tests: Integration-style jest tests only (tests/KV.test.js, tests/PKI*.test.js, tests/LDAP.test.js, tests/Userpass.test.js, tests/AD-*.test.js, tests/TOTP.test.js, tests/SysApi.test.js, ...), each instantiating Vault from VAULT_URL and real tokens in tests/process.env; no unit test asserts the constructed request URL, and the library itself needs no network beyond Vault.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap only the KV secret name (and maybe the version) in encodeURIComponent inside readKVSecret, treating the report's two examples as the whole affected surface and leaving the other 48 methods' concatenation untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The class stores a raw axios client as a public property (src/Vault.js:145) that every method calls with an arbitrary Options.url; callers can bypass the method-level path building entirely, but that is a transport escape hatch rather than a missing encoding site, so it is not counted as an O2 site.
